subject: SCIENCE
title: Family Traits
objective: Compare inherited traits using fictional organisms.
introduction: A baby frog looks like its parents, but not exactly. Which traits do young ones get from their parents?

vocabulary.definition: Everything around us — land, water, and air.
A feature or quality a living thing has.
A living thing that can move, like a dog or bird.

items.prompt: Which statement about inherited traits is true?

options.text: Offspring can inherit traits but are not exact copies; traits can involve genes and environment.

items.explanation: Young animals and plants get traits from their parents but are not exact copies — the environment can shape them too.

items.prompt: Which trait could a young animal be born with?
items.explanation: The beetle's color pattern comes from its parents, so it is inherited. Scars and haircuts come from what happens to the animal, not from its parents.

items.prompt: Which statement about offspring is NOT true?

options.text: Young ones are born with traits from their parents.
Traits can be shaped by the environment.
Offspring are always exact copies of a parent.

items.explanation: Young ones get traits from their parents but are not exact copies — each one is unique. They are born with traits, and the environment can shape them.

items.prompt: Which is true?  (in this lesson: Family Traits)

options.text: Offspring may resemble parents without being exact copies.

items.explanation: Young ones often look like their parents but are not exactly the same — each individual is unique.

items.prompt: Which trait could an animal be born with?

options.text: a song a cartoon animal learned
a toy a cartoon animal plays with

items.explanation: Fur pattern comes from the animal's parents, so it is inherited. Toys and learned songs are not born with the animal.
